assessment: This article will interest neuroscientists who study how spinal circuits control locomotion. While the role of spinal interneurons in control of left–right and flexor–extensor alternations has been studied extensively, their role in hind–forelimb coordination has not been sufficiently studied. Zhang et al. study interlimb coordination by combining experimental data and computer simulation to shed light on how a population of spinal neurons may coordinate hind and fore limbs during locomotion at different speeds.
